entries.critique: The page renders cleanly at this viewport: header bar, theme toggle, left nav (Foundations/Components & Chrome/Brand & Voice groups), and main content all have clear spacing and hierarchy. The intro callout card, section headers ("PART 1", "Foundations", "Color"), and the three color-family tables (Brand & Unthemed, Ground & Surfaces, Text Ink) are aligned and legible with no visible clipping, overlap, or text truncation. Nothing is cut off at the right or bottom edge of the viewport in what's captured.

entries.surface_description: The public living styleguide at its opening position.
entries.critique: This is the design-system styleguide's opening view (Foundations → Color) in night mode. Page-level text is legible throughout: the large white heading, the light-gray body copy on the near-black background, the sidebar nav (active "Color" item shown with a clear violet highlight and white text, inactive items in a lighter gray that still reads against the dark ground), the purple callout card's bold "Not sure? Start here" heading and its body text with inline code tokens, and the section headers "PART 1 / Foundations / Color" all sit at comfortable contrast against the dark theme. The color-token swatches (Brand & Unthemed, Ground & Surfaces, Text Ink) intentionally render each chip in its actual token color with the value printed on it — including light chips like --on-brand (#fff) and --surface (#ffffff) — and each keeps readable dark-on-light or light-on-dark text; that is the swatch doing its job of showing the literal color, not a night-mode contrast failure. No glyph, label, or control in this frame is illegible or unlocatable.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique: The feedback form card is well-composed internally (clear heading, tab toggle, textarea, checkbox, disclaimer, CTA, and a purple "What happens next" aside all sit with sensible spacing and legible contrast). However, at this 1376×1032 landscape viewport the card is sized for a much narrower/portrait layout and left-aligned near the top, leaving roughly two-thirds of the screen below and to the right as flat empty gray space. No element is clipped, overlapping, or mis-fit, but the layout doesn't adapt to the available width/height, producing a lopsided, unbalanced composition on a large landscape display.
entries.recommendation: On wide/landscape viewports, either cap-and-center the card vertically as well as horizontally, or introduce a responsive max-width/height with balanced margins so the form doesn't read as a small island in a mostly empty page.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique: In night mode, the active tab label "Something's broken" and its container use a muted dark-gray on dark-gray combination that is noticeably lower contrast than surrounding UI text (the heading, body copy, and "What happens next" panel all read crisply). The checkbox label "Include device info (helps us reproduce the bug)" and the helper text below it ("Your report goes to our private support tracker...") are also rendered in a dimmed gray that is legible but sits well below the contrast level of the rest of the form's text, making it the weakest-reading text on the page outside of placeholder text.
entries.recommendation: Increase the text color contrast of the tab labels and the checkbox/helper text against the dark background to match the contrast level used elsewhere in the form (e.g., closer to the body paragraph's light gray rather than a dimmer secondary tone).

Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: The public privacy policy at its opening position.
entries.critique: In dark/night mode, the privacy policy page shows strong, legible contrast throughout: the white heading and body text, the light-gray intro paragraph, the bordered "short version" summary card with its colored dot markers and bold lead-in words, the sidebar navigation (active item highlighted with a purple-tinted background and left accent bar, inactive items in readable gray), and the "THE DETAILS" body copy all read clearly against the near-black background. No thinning/scrim/scroll-fade artifacts or clipped elements are visible in this capture, and no low-contrast issue affects any element outside the two controls (chevron/settings) that are explicitly out of scope as intentionally subdued.

entries.surface_description: Google Play closed-test instructions, on the Android tab of the beta page.
entries.critique: Page hierarchy, spacing, and text fit are clean throughout the visible content: heading, intro copy, tabs, and numbered steps 1–3 all have clear structure with no overlap or crowding. The one flaw is at the bottom edge: the step-3 "Open Splotch on Google Play" button is sliced off partway down, with the visible portion also rendered at reduced opacity/lighter purple than the other two step buttons. This does not match the app's documented scroll-fade convention (a soft gradient fade painted over the last element) — here the button is hard-cropped by the frame edge with no gradient easing, so it reads as an accidental clip rather than an intentional "more content below" cue. Since this is a static page (not a modal/dialog with scrim), there's no indication whether this is a genuine scroll region continuing below, or the capture simply ends before the content does.
entries.recommendation: If content continues below step 3, apply the same soft gradient fade treatment used elsewhere for scrollable regions along this bottom edge so the cutoff reads as an intentional continuation cue rather than clipped content; if this is the true end of the page, ensure the final button and any following spacing render at full opacity and are not truncated by the viewport.

entries.surface_description: Google Play closed-test instructions, on the Android tab of the beta page.
entries.critique: In the Android instructions list, step 3 ("Install Splotch") — its numbered circle, heading, body copy, and the "Open Splotch on Google Play" button — renders at noticeably reduced opacity/contrast compared to steps 1 and 2, which are fully bright. The button's white label text is especially hard to read against the dimmed purple fill. This dimming affects the entire step block uniformly rather than thinning out toward a boundary, so it doesn't match the described scroll-fade cue, and step 3 is not an Actions Panel control governed by the undo/AI/screenshot disabled-state rule, so no documented exception explains it.
entries.recommendation: Render step 3 (heading, body text, numbered circle, and the "Open Splotch on Google Play" button) at the same full opacity/contrast as steps 1 and 2, so its button label meets legible contrast against the purple fill.

entries.surface_description: TestFlight instructions, on the iOS tab of the beta page.
entries.critique: Hierarchy, spacing, and text fit within the content column are clean: numbered steps, headings, body copy, and CTA buttons are all legible with no clipping, overlap, or touch-target ambiguity. However, at this 1376px landscape width the content column occupies only about 60% of the viewport, leaving a large empty gray margin on the right side of the page for its entire length. The layout reads as a narrow mobile/tablet-portrait column simply left-aligned inside a much wider frame rather than a design adapted to iPad landscape.
entries.recommendation: Constrain the content to a centered max-width column (or introduce a second column / wider card padding) so the page composition uses the available landscape width instead of leaving roughly 40% of the viewport as unused whitespace.

entries.surface_description: TestFlight instructions, on the iOS tab of the beta page.
entries.critique: On the iOS TestFlight instructions tab in night mode, the numbered step badges (1, 2, 3) are rendered as dark reddish/olive digits on a barely-lighter dark circular background, both very close in luminance to the page background. They are legible only at close inspection and read as much fainter than the surrounding step titles, body text, and purple CTA buttons, which are all high-contrast. This is a genuine numbered-list index and not one of the parent-facing controls or scrim/fade cases called out as expected low-contrast styling, so the weak contrast here looks like an unaddressed night-mode legibility gap rather than intentional restraint.
entries.recommendation: Increase the contrast of the step-number badges in dark mode, e.g. a lighter fill or brighter digit color, so the numerals are clearly readable at a glance against the dark background.

entries.surface_description: The shared SvelteKit error boundary rendered for an unknown route.
entries.critique: The error boundary renders cleanly on iPad Pro 13" landscape at 1376×1032. Content is centered in the viewport with generous surrounding whitespace, no clipping or overlap. Hierarchy is clear: purple blob icon, bold "Oops!" heading, muted gray body text, and a solid purple pill "Start over" button. The button is comfortably sized (~153×48px) well above minimum touch-target guidelines. Text wraps cleanly to two lines with no truncation. No modal/scrim is present since this is a full-page error state, not an overlay, so none of the scrim/fade/disabled-state design context applies here. Nothing about this view suggests an actionable issue.

entries.critique: This capture shows the tablet split-pane Settings dialog (Appearance panel) on iPad Pro 13" landscape, not the compact phone-landscape shell, so the Portrait/Landscape rotation-lock segments described in the design intent aren't present here to assess. Within what is visible: the scrim correctly dims and blurs the canvas, palette, and corner buttons behind the modal while the dialog itself stays crisp; sidebar nav items have clear icons, labels, and an active-state highlight on "Appearance"; the Light/Dark/System segmented control is legible with a clear selected state; toggles (Lock device rotation off, Sound/Drawing on) are unambiguous; the "Deleting" row at the bottom is thinning/fading into the bottom edge, consistent with the documented scroll-fade cue rather than a clipping defect. No overlap, clipping, or unreadable text is present in the unfaded content.

entries.recommendation: Add a small visible gap or drop shadow between the brush flyout and the Actions Panel below it so the two surfaces read as distinct layers rather than one fused card.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique: The honeycomb color-grid card floats with no header, title, or close/dismiss control anywhere in its bounds — just the hexagon grid with a white ring marking the current selection (top-right cell). There is no visible "X," done button, or affordance to exit the picker short of tapping a swatch or presumably tapping outside the card, and neither of those is discoverable from the image alone. Aside from that, the grid itself reads cleanly: hexagons are evenly sized and spaced, the gradient across hue/lightness is legible, the selected white cell has a clear dark outline, and the scrim behind (canvas, left-edge swatch rail, corner buttons) is uniformly dimmed/blurred with the card in sharp focus, consistent with this app's modal pattern. No clipping, overlap, or text-fit problems are visible since the card contains no text at all.
entries.recommendation: Add a visible close/done affordance (X or button) to the honeycomb color-picker card so users aren't left guessing how to dismiss it.

entries.surface_description: The in-place row expansion on phones and inline actions on tablets.
entries.critique: In the access-codes table's Actions column, "Copy" and "Copy link" are rendered as bordered buttons with bright purple/white text, but "Remove" is plain gray text with no border, sitting at markedly lower contrast against the dark row background. It's still legible, so it clears the findability floor, but it reads noticeably weaker than its sibling actions in the same row, which is inconsistent given all three are equally destructive/important row actions (not a disabled or secondary state per the app's documented patterns).
entries.recommendation: Increase the text color contrast of the "Remove" link (or give it a subtle outline like Copy/Copy link) so it reads at a similar contrast level to the other row actions in night mode.
